newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak leaves unexpectedly for G-15 meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak leaves unexpectedly for G-15 meeting.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak left Cairo for Harare on Saturday to attend a Group of 15 meeting on the trade concerns of developing countries.
Egypt had not announced in advance that Mubarak would go to the meeting, apparently for security reasons.

Mubarak has not travelled south of Egypt since Islamist militants tried to kill him in July 1995 as he arrived in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa for a summit meeting of the Organisation of African Unity,

The organisers of the Group of 15 meeting said on Friday that eight heads of state and government had so far confirmed their attendance at the November 3 to 5 summit but they declined to name them, citing security reasons.

The leaders will map out strategies for promoting trade between them and for stimulating growth in the world's poorest regions. The summit will look at ways of forging a common front among African, Asian and Latin American states to give them a stronger voice in a world moving towards free trade.
"By far trade issues are going to top the agenda of the meeting," said Tichaona Jokonya, Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe's special representative to the Group of 15.
The members of the group are Algeria, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Jamaica, Malaysia, Nigeria, Senegal, Peru, Venezuela, Yugoslavia and Zimbabwe.
